propositions: _gc_pass reads only free disk space and entry mtime, never consulting the incrementally-maintained byte_total, so the ADR-promised byte-total backstop trigger does not exist.
materialize_tickets bypasses cache.acquire and never calls add_bytes, leaving its ~620 MiB entries unaccounted in the store's byte total despite being the dominant consumer.
The snapshot store lacks a configurable size cap knob in the config surface, leaving only the free-space watermark and max-age cold-trim as eviction triggers.
Real-world conditions show materialize_tickets entries (~861 MiB each, ~1.7 GiB for two entries) contribute zero to byte_total while dominating the 47+ GiB store.
A byte-total-driven eviction trigger with cap and target margin must be added to _gc_pass to implement the promised backstop.
materialize_tickets must record its entries by calling add_bytes so the incremental counter reflects actual store size.
